## Setup

Let $g=3$ and $n=12$. Write $\mathcal{M}_{3,12}$ for the moduli stack of smooth genus-$3$ curves with $12$ distinct ordered marked points, and $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{3,12}$ for its Deligne–Mumford compactification. Both are smooth Deligne–Mumford stacks over $\mathbb{C}$. The dimension is
$$
d \;=\; 3g-3+n \;=\; 18.
$$
All cohomology and Borel–Moore homology are with rational coefficients; weight filtrations are Deligne’s (extended in the usual way to smooth DM stacks).

By purity for smooth proper DM stacks, $H^k(\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{3,12})$ is pure of weight $k$ (THM-0001). For even $k\le 14$, this pure Hodge structure is a direct sum of Tate twists $\mathbb{Q}(-k/2)$ for every stable pair (THM-0002). Degree $16$ remains open (CONJ-0001, OBS-0001).

**Approach.** Prove only the weaker pure-weight Tate statement for the open Borel–Moore input at $(3,12)$, without CKgP, algebraicity of cycles, or tautological generation on $\mathcal{M}_{3,12}$ (packet execution boundary; FND-0002).

## Duality and exact target

Poincaré duality for a smooth DM stack of dimension $d=18$ identifies
$$
H^{BM}_k(\mathcal{M}_{3,12})
\;\simeq\;
H^{2d-k}(\mathcal{M}_{3,12})(d)
\;=\;
H^{36-k}(\mathcal{M}_{3,12})(18).
$$
Weights are compatible, so
$$
W_{-16}\,H^{BM}_{16}(\mathcal{M}_{3,12})
\;\simeq\;
W_{20}\,H^{20}(\mathcal{M}_{3,12})(18)
$$
(FND-0001, RED-0001).

**Target.** The finite obstruction list for compact degree $16$ includes $(g,n)=(3,12)$. The required pure-weight statement is
$$
W_{-16}\,H^{BM}_{16}(\mathcal{M}_{3,12})
\quad\text{pure of Tate type}\quad
\mathbb{Q}(8).
$$
Equivalently, untwisted ordinary cohomology satisfies
$$
W_{20}\,H^{20}(\mathcal{M}_{3,12})
\quad\text{pure of Tate type}\quad
\mathbb{Q}(-10),
$$
since $\mathbb{Q}(-10)(18)=\mathbb{Q}(8)$. The associated Chow codimension, if algebraic, would be $d-8=10$. We do **not** claim algebraicity.

## Reduction from compact degree 16

The boundary right-exact sequence of the low-homology induction (THM-0003) yields
$$
H_{16}(\partial\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{3,12})
\;\longrightarrow\;
H_{16}(\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{3,12})
\;\longrightarrow\;
W_{-16}\,H^{BM}_{16}(\mathcal{M}_{3,12})
\;\longrightarrow\; 0.
$$
Thus $W_{-16}\,H^{BM}_{16}(\mathcal{M}_{3,12})$ is the pure-weight open quotient of compact homology in degree $16$.

The base-case inequalities (THM-0004) at $k=16$, $g=3$, $n=12\ge 2$ require an open-stratum base case precisely when
$$
k \;\ge\; 2g-2+n \;=\; 16.
$$
Equality holds, so $(3,12)$ is a genuine open base case. The compact pure-Tate statement $H^{16}(\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{3,12})\simeq \bigoplus \mathbb{Q}(-8)$ therefore reduces, for this pair, to
$$
W_{-16}\,H^{BM}_{16}(\mathcal{M}_{3,12})\;\simeq\; \bigoplus\, \mathbb{Q}(8),
$$
once boundary strata are controlled inductively (even degrees $\le 14$ by THM-0002; genus $1$ and $2$ by THM-0006–THM-0007).

## Forgetful generation from the CKgP range $n\le 11$

Published CKgP bounds give $c(3)=11$ (THM-0005): for every $m\le 11$, $\mathcal{M}_{3,m}$ has CKgP and tautological Chow ring, so pure-weight cohomology/BM of $\mathcal{M}_{3,m}$ is algebraic Tate of the expected type.

For each $i\in\{1,\dots,12\}$, the forgetful map $\pi_i\colon \mathcal{M}_{3,12}\to\mathcal{M}_{3,11}$ is smooth of relative dimension $1$ and weight-compatible on cohomology. Pullbacks therefore embed a pure-Tate subspace
$$
\sum_{i=1}^{12}\pi_i^*\bigl(W_{20}H^{20}(\mathcal{M}_{3,11})\bigr)
\;\subset\;
W_{20}H^{20}(\mathcal{M}_{3,12})
$$
of type $\mathbb{Q}(-10)$, and more generally all pure-weight classes pulled back from $m\le 11$ (together with tautological $\psi$-classes on the twelve marks) remain pure Tate.

This does **not** prove generation of the whole pure-weight piece: the forgetful system from $n\le 11$ need not exhaust $W_{20}H^{20}(\mathcal{M}_{3,12})$. CKgP for $\mathcal{M}_{3,12}$ itself is unknown (THM-0005 stops at $c(3)=11$), and the ordered twelve-point cubic incidence locus is not known to be CKgP by permanence lemmas (FND-0002). The present approach does not use any CKgP extension to $n=12$.

## Hyperelliptic / plane-quartic stratification

Every smooth genus-$3$ curve is hyperelliptic or non-hyperelliptic; in the latter case the canonical system embeds it as a smooth plane quartic. Stratify
$$
\mathcal{M}_{3,12}
\;=\;
\mathcal{H}_{3,12}
\;\sqcup\;
\mathcal{Q}_{3,12},
$$
where $\mathcal{H}_{3,12}$ is the ordered $12$-pointed hyperelliptic locus and $\mathcal{Q}_{3,12}$ the non-hyperelliptic (plane-quartic) open locus.

The unpointed hyperelliptic locus $\mathcal{H}_3\subset\mathcal{M}_3$ is a divisor ($\dim\mathcal{M}_3=6$, $\dim\mathcal{H}_3=5$). After marking twelve points, $\mathcal{H}_{3,12}$ is a pure-dimensional closed stratum of dimension $17$ in the smooth locus, with open complement $\mathcal{Q}_{3,12}$ of dimension $18$.

**Hyperelliptic side.** Hyperelliptic genus-$3$ curves are double covers of $\mathbb{P}^1$ branched at eight points. The pointed stack $\mathcal{H}_{3,12}$ is built from configuration spaces of branch points and marks on $\mathbb{P}^1$ with residual $\mathrm{PGL}_2$-action, hence from genus-$0$ data. Genus $0$ has unrestricted CKgP (THM-0005) and pure-weight Tate cohomology. After stacky automorphisms of the hyperelliptic involution, contributions of $\mathcal{H}_{3,12}$ to $W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(\mathcal{M}_{3,12})$ via BM localization are expected to be of type $\mathbb{Q}(8)$ (or zero).

**Plane-quartic side.** A point of $\mathcal{Q}_{3,12}$ is a smooth plane quartic with twelve ordered points. The pure-weight group $W_{20}H^{20}(\mathcal{Q}_{3,12})$ (equivalently $W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(\mathcal{Q}_{3,12})$) is the main geometric unknown for the open dense stratum.

**Localization.** The BM localization sequence in degree $16$ reads
$$
\cdots
\to
H^{BM}_{16}(\mathcal{H}_{3,12})
\to
H^{BM}_{16}(\mathcal{M}_{3,12})
\to
H^{BM}_{16}(\mathcal{Q}_{3,12})
\to
H^{BM}_{15}(\mathcal{H}_{3,12})
\to
\cdots.
$$
Passing to $W_{-16}$, kernel and cokernel of the comparison between $W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(\mathcal{M}_{3,12})$ and $W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(\mathcal{Q}_{3,12})$ are controlled by pure-weight BM of $\mathcal{H}_{3,12}$. If both the hyperelliptic pure-weight groups in the relevant degrees and $W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(\mathcal{Q}_{3,12})$ are of type $\mathbb{Q}(8)$, the same follows for $\mathcal{M}_{3,12}$.

Thus the pure-weight Tate problem reduces to: (i) a genus-$0$/configuration-space computation on $\mathcal{H}_{3,12}$; (ii) a pure-weight computation on $\mathcal{Q}_{3,12}$ that does **not** require CKgP of the ordered cubic-incidence geometry (FND-0002).

## What is established

1. **Target identification.** With $d=18$, $W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(\mathcal{M}_{3,12})\simeq W_{20}H^{20}(\mathcal{M}_{3,12})(18)$, with matching Tate types $\mathbb{Q}(8)$ vs $\mathbb{Q}(-10)$ (FND-0001, RED-0001).
2. **Compact-to-open reduction.** Via THM-0003 and the equality $16=2g-2+n$ (THM-0004), compact pure Tate at $(3,12)$ reduces to pure Tate type $\mathbb{Q}(8)$ for the open pure-weight BM group.
3. **CKgP range.** For $m\le 11$, pure-weight cohomology is algebraic Tate (THM-0005); forgetful pullbacks inject a pure-Tate subspace into $W_{20}H^{20}(\mathcal{M}_{3,12})$.
4. **Stratification framework.** Hyperelliptic/plane-quartic decomposition plus BM localization is a valid pure-weight setup that does not presuppose CKgP on $\mathcal{M}_{3,12}$ (FND-0002).
5. **Scope.** Pure-weight Tate is strictly weaker than CKgP/algebraicity and is allowed by the packet boundary; no algebraicity claim is made.

## Explicit gaps

**GAP-1 (Forgetful generation).** It is not proved that pullbacks from $\mathcal{M}_{3,m}$ for $m\le 11$ (plus tautological $\psi/\kappa$) exhaust $W_{20}H^{20}(\mathcal{M}_{3,12})$. A complementary non-Tate summand is not ruled out.

**GAP-2 (Hyperelliptic pure weight).** The identification of $W_{-*}H^{BM}_*(\mathcal{H}_{3,12})$ with equivariant genus-$0$ configuration cohomology, including hyperelliptic stack structure and the exact contribution to $W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(\mathcal{M}_{3,12})$, is not fully verified.

**GAP-3 (Plane-quartic pure weight).** It is not proved that $W_{20}H^{20}(\mathcal{Q}_{3,12})$ has type $\mathbb{Q}(-10)$, equivalently that $W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(\mathcal{Q}_{3,12})$ has type $\mathbb{Q}(8)$. This is the main geometric gap.

**GAP-4 (Incidence without CKgP).** Resolving GAP-3 via ordered twelve-point cubic incidence cannot use CKgP: permanence lemmas do not establish CKgP there, nor ascent from the unordered stack along the finite étale ordering cover (FND-0002). No pure-weight substitute (weight spectral sequence, cell stratification, vanishing of wrong-weight graded pieces) is supplied.

**GAP-5 (Localization weights).** Even granting Tate-ness on $\mathcal{H}_{3,12}$ and $\mathcal{Q}_{3,12}$ separately, absence of non-Tate extensions or weight-shifted terms in the BM sequence in degrees $15$–$16$ is not checked with complete vanishing ranges.

**GAP-6 (Boundary bookkeeping).** Line-by-line verification that every dual graph for $\partial\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{3,12}$ lands in already-known pure-Tate cases at degree $16$ is not reproduced; it is treated as ambient inductive machine rather than a fresh check.

## Conclusion

The open-input target, duality, degrees ($d=18$, ordinary degree $20$, types $\mathbb{Q}(8)$ and $\mathbb{Q}(-10)$), and a pure-weight-without-CKgP strategy via forgetful maps and hyperelliptic/plane-quartic stratification are correctly set up. GAP-1–GAP-6 block any claim that $W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(\mathcal{M}_{3,12})$ is of Tate type $\mathbb{Q}(8)$. Status of the attempt: incomplete proposed reduction only.
assumptions: Rational singular and Borel–Moore (co)homology of smooth DM stacks carry mixed Hodge structures compatible with localization and forgetful morphisms as in the published low-homology induction.

Boundary dual-graph strata for Mbar_{3,12} in degree 16 fall under the ambient inductive control once open base cases are settled (standard shape of THM-0003–THM-0004; not re-verified graph-by-graph here).
Genus-0 pure-weight cohomology is Tate, as implied by unrestricted CKgP in genus 0 (THM-0005).

claims.statement: With d=18, Poincare duality gives W_{-16} H^{BM}_{16}(M_{3,12}) ≅ W_{20} H^{20}(M_{3,12})(18), so the BM group is of Tate type Q(8) if and only if the untwisted ordinary pure-weight group is of Tate type Q(-10).

By the boundary right-exact sequence and the base-case inequality k=16=2g-2+n, the pure-Tate statement for H^{16}(Mbar_{3,12}) at this pair reduces to pure Tate type Q(8) for W_{-16} H^{BM}_{16}(M_{3,12}), once boundary strata are inductively controlled.
For all m≤c(3)=11, M_{3,m} has CKgP, so pure-weight cohomology of M_{3,m} is algebraic of Tate type; forgetful pullbacks embed a pure-Tate subspace of type Q(-10) into W_{20} H^{20}(M_{3,12}).

The hyperelliptic/plane-quartic stratification M_{3,12}=H_{3,12} ⊔ Q_{3,12} together with the BM localization sequence in degree 16 reduces the pure-weight Tate problem to pure-weight control of H_{3,12} (genus-0 type) and of Q_{3,12}, without presupposing CKgP on M_{3,12}.
Pullbacks from M_{3,m} for m≤11 together with tautological psi/kappa classes generate all of W_{20} H^{20}(M_{3,12}).
W_{-16} H^{BM}_{16}(H_{3,12}) (and the associated localization contributions in degrees 15–16) is pure of Tate type Q(8) or zero.
W_{20} H^{20}(Q_{3,12}) is pure of Tate type Q(-10), equivalently W_{-16} H^{BM}_{16}(Q_{3,12}) is pure of Tate type Q(8).
W_{-16} H^{BM}_{16}(M_{3,12}) is pure of Tate type Q(8).

GAP-2: hyperelliptic pure-weight BM computation not fully carried out
GAP-3: plane-quartic pure-weight Tate for Q_{3,12} unproved
GAP-4: ordered cubic incidence cannot be used via CKgP (FND-0002); no pure-weight substitute supplied
GAP-5: BM localization weight comparison in degrees 15–16 incomplete
GAP-6: boundary dual-graph bookkeeping at degree 16 not re-verified line-by-line
summary: Partial pure-weight Tate reduction for (g,n)=(3,12): dualizes W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{3,12}) to W_{20}H^{20}(M_{3,12})(18), uses forgetful CKgP range n<=11 and a hyperelliptic/plane-quartic stratification, but leaves the plane-quartic pure-weight and generation gaps open.
